plan:
x is viewed as (B, C, HW/128, 128) (layout only) so a channel is a (128, 128) slab of 16 vregs on a leading, untiled dim;
rows of 16384 lanes would make each 8-channel group a 128-vreg value (spills, long lane-reduce chains).
Grid (B, C // CB) with ~4 MiB blocks (fewer steps, vmem_limit raised); an unrolled fori_loop over the CB channels of a block.
Per channel: sum over sublanes (VPU vreg adds) then one lane reduce, var = E[x^2] - E[x]^2, a = scale * rsqrt(var + eps).
Then out = x * a + (shift - mean * a) straight from VMEM; scale/shift are f32 scalars in SMEM, so x is read once from HBM.

Grid (B, C/8): x passed W/128 times, each spec a (1, 8, H, 128) block of one 128-lane column chunk (2 MB each, 16 MB double-buffered).
Per channel: stride-4 sublane loads + max give the 4-row pool per chunk; an XLU transpose, a 128-lane scratch and stride-4 loads give the
4-column pool; the 4 chunks concatenate into the (128,128) base map. The four padded 2x2 stages reuse the scratch with -inf margins
(data at row offset 8, so pad=1 is a stride-2 load starting at row 7) and transposes for the column direction; each stage is stored.
f32 throughout (max is exact). One HBM pass over x; no lane-strided or non-128-lane strided access (Mosaic cannot lower those).

a small pack pallas_call turns each bf16 row (256) into one 512 B int32 row (128 words: col j low half, col j+128 high
half), so every gathered row is a single contiguous 32-bit DMA at half the bytes, not 1 KiB two-segment row DMAs; no float math outside any kernel (an outside f32 cast would be an extra 96 MiB pass).
main grid (nb/tb + 2,) "arbitrary", tb=2048, 3-slot int32 scratch: step i issues block i's row DMAs while unpacking block i-2
(shift/mask -> f32 bitcast -> exact bf16) in the same 16-row loop, so vector work and DMA latency hide behind DMA issue.
out/binary block index max(i-2,0) (visited consecutively, written once); the binary copy is fused into the same loop.

Grid (B, H/Hb), Hb=16: blocks (1,128,16,256) f32 = 2 MB per input, double-buffered 8 MB. No reshape outside.
Pass 1 (fori over C): f32 sums of s^2 and t^2 per pixel -> inverse norms 1/max(sqrt, eps). Pass 2 (fori over C, same VMEM block):
accumulate (s*is - t*it)^2 into a (Hb,W) carry, added to a (Hb,W) f32 scratch. Last step: full reduce -> (1,128); [0,0] outside.
Speed idea: single HBM read of 268 MB; the second channel pass re-reads VMEM only.

Grid (T/8,) sequential; k, v blocks (8, B, 256) bf16 (512 KiB each); q and weights as constant full blocks.
Per step: one (8*B, K) x (K, H) bf16 matmul with f32 accumulation, f32 tanh, logits via two bf16 matmuls (column form for the
online-softmax value sum, NT row form stored into a (T, B) f32 scratch); m/l/acc online-softmax state in f32 scratch.
Last step: acc/l to the (1, B, V) output and a full softmax over the stored logits, transposed in-kernel to the (B, T) output.
Outside: only bias reshapes/astype, a pad and broadcast of out_w (layout ops); out_b cancels in the softmax.
Speed idea: 64 MXU-sized steps rather than 512 serial tiny ones; no HIGHEST passes.

Grid (B*J/64,) "arbitrary"; pred/gt blocks (64, H, W) bf16 = 2 MiB each over the bitcast view (B*J, H, W).
Per-plane weights as f32 scalars in SMEM; full (B, J) f32 weight block in VMEM for sum(target_weight).
fori_loop over planes, 32-row chunks: d = (gt-pred)^2*w, smooth d>thr as exp(0.1*log d)*thr^0.9, fold into an (8, W) f32 carry.
Accumulator (8, W) f32 scratch; last step writes sum / (H*W*max(1, sum w)) as (1,1). Outside: bitcast reshapes, astype only.

Grid (rows/br,) "arbitrary" over the free view (B*C*H, W); blocks (br, W) of fake and real, br*W*4 = 4 MB.
f32 scratch (8, W): per step add sum over row-groups of |scale*real - scale*fake| with plain vreg adds.
Last step: full reduce of the partial divided by numel into a (1,1) output; outside only the bitcast reshape and [0,0].
Speed idea: no relayout copies of the inputs, one HBM pass, no per-step cross-lane reduce.

Grid (B*C/bn,) over (B*C, H, W) views of x and y (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); blocks (bn, H, W) f32 of 4 MB each (bn=16).
Inside: fori over the bn images, static 32-row chunks: sqrt((x-y)^2 + eps^2) folded into an (8, W) f32 carry.
Accumulator: (8, W) f32 VMEM scratch resident across the "arbitrary" grid; the last step reduces it and multiplies by 1/N.
Outside: only the bitcast reshapes and the (1,1) -> scalar reshape.
Speed idea: a (rows, 1024) flatten would cost two 268 MB relayout copies; the native layout makes it one 268 MB HBM pass.

Grid (N, C/cb) both arbitrary, block (1, cb, H, W) f32 on the native 4D arrays, cb=16 -> 2 MiB per input, 64 steps.
Inner fori_loop over (channel, 32-row chunk); |log r - log f| folded into an (8, W) f32 carry, added to a VMEM scratch.
Last step reduces the scratch to (1,1) and scales by 1/size; only reshape(()) and astype stay outside.
Speed: no reshape that changes the last dim, so no relayout copies (those would add 512 MB of traffic).

Grid (N, H/hb) = (8, 16), block (1, C, hb, W) = (1, 128, 16, 256) f32 = 2 MiB on the native NCHW layout (no reshape).
Channel fori_loop accumulates x^2 into an (hb, W) f32 vreg carry; inv = 1/(sqrt+eps) once; second channel loop writes x * (inv * w[c]).
weight in SMEM as (C,) f32 scalars; nothing else outside the kernel.
Speed idea: one read and one write, channel reduction is plain vreg adds, no relayout copies.

Call 1: grid (N0,), block x (1,N1,N2,N3) bf16; f32 sum of squares over the leading axis 1, R = 1/(sqrt+eps) -> (1,N2,N3) f32.
Outside: T = R.transpose(2,0,1) on the 1 MB f32 array (layout op only).
Call 2: grid (N0,), x block (1,N1,N2,N3), T block (1,N2,N1); static loop over b: out[0,b] = x[0,b] * T[0][:, b:b+1] (lane broadcast).
f32 math, bf16 store. Speed idea: ~96 MB of HBM traffic total instead of a 32 MB transposed copy plus two reads.

an x.reshape(rows, 1024) would change the minor (lane) dim, which on TPU's tiled HBM layout forces a full
128 MiB relayout copy (read+write) before the kernel; so only leading dims are merged: x -> (B*C, H, W), a free bitcast.
grid over blocks of (bb, H, W) with H, W full dims (~4 MiB bf16, 32 steps, "arbitrary"); fori_loop over bb on the
untiled leading dim, relu+square in bf16 (as the reference does), upcast and add into a (64, W) f32 carry = 16 independent vreg chains.
(64, W) f32 VMEM scratch persists across steps (zeroed at step 0); last step does full sum + sqrt in-kernel; outside only reshape/astype.

Three chained 2x2/2 VALID max pools are the same as one 8x8/8 VALID max pool.
Outside the kernel: slice x to multiples of 8 and reshape it to (N*C, Ho, 8, W). The grid runs over groups of b=8 images; the input block is (b, Ho, 8, W) f32 (2 MiB), so no strided loads are needed.
In the kernel: max over axis 2 (a sublane reduction) gives (b*Ho, W). Transpose that to (W, b*Ho), reshape to (Wo, 8, b*Ho) and take the max over axis 1, giving a lane-dense (Wo, b*Ho) output block.
Outside, a layout-only reshape and transpose of the small pooled output gives (N, C, Ho, Wo). The kernel is bandwidth bound: it reads x once.

Grid (B,), one full (1, C, H, W) bf16 image per step (4 MB in + 4 MB out, double-buffered, 96 MB VMEM limit); no reshapes of x, so no relayout copies.
Pass 1 (in VMEM): per-channel sum and sum of squares in f32, 8 channels per fori_loop iteration so 8 reduction chains overlap; results lane-broadcast into (C,128) scratch.
Layer stats from the channel sums; one vectorized step builds per-channel scale a and shift b mixing IN and LN by rho, times gamma, plus beta.
Pass 2: out = x*a + b, 8 channels per iteration, cast to bf16 on store.
Outside: only reshape/astype of the (1,C,1,1) parameters to (C,1) f32.

Outside: x.reshape(n, c*h, w) and out back to (n, c, h, w) (bitcasts: only leading dims merge); gamma/beta to f32 (c,) in SMEM.
Grid (n,), one whole sample per step: block (1, c*h, w) bf16 = 16 MiB in + 16 MiB out, double buffered (vmem limit 100 MiB).
Pass 1 over row chunks (one channel slice of rc rows each): f32 sum and sum of squares into (8, w) accumulators.
Pass 2: y = x * (gamma*rstd) + (beta - mean*gamma*rstd) per channel, f32 math, bf16 store.
Speed idea: x is read from HBM once (XLA reads it twice), and no relayout copies.

Pass 1 grid (R/1024,) over x viewed as (R, F) (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); block (1024, F) f32; (8, F) f32 VMEM accumulator of x*x, reduced to (1,1) at the last step.
Pass 2 grid (R/1024,) "parallel"; block (1024, F); per-row mean and unbiased variance on the whole block at once, scale = sqrt(4F/S)/(std+eps).
All math in float32; outside the kernels only reshape.
Speed idea: whole-block vector ops (no 8-row fori_loop) so the passes are HBM-bound: 3 x 268 MB total, the minimum for a global-sum-dependent normalize.

Grid (N, H/th), block (1, C, th, W) f32 with th chosen so a block is ~2 MiB (128 x 32 x 128 here); weight/bias broadcast outside to (C, 8, W) and resident (constant index map).
Inside: fori_loop over 8-row chunks; per chunk (C, 8, W) the channel mean and variance are sums over the major axis (vreg adds), all in f32.
Nothing outside the kernel except the broadcast of weight/bias; x is never reshaped, so no relayout copies.
Speed idea: single HBM pass (268 MB) versus XLA's multi-fusion layer norm, and without the two relayout copies a reshaped layout would cost.

Grid (N, H/th) over the untouched NCHW array; block (1, C, th, W) = (1, 256, 32, 128) f32, 4 MB in + 4 MB out.
No reshape: merging H into lanes would force an HBM relayout of input and output (3x the traffic).
C is a major dim of the block, so mean and variance are fori_loops of (th, W) vreg adds over channels (two-pass
variance, f32), then rsqrt; a third loop writes (x-u)*a*gamma[c] + beta[c] with gamma/beta read as SMEM scalars.
All per-channel work is 4 vregs, so nothing spills; only the HBM stream (537 MB) should matter.

Grid (N,): one whole sample per step as a (1, C*H, W) f32 block (8 MB) of the bitcast view (N, C*H, W); output block the same.
In VMEM: pass 1 sums x*x over 256-row chunks into an (8, W) f32 value; scale = 1/sqrt(sum/m + eps); pass 2 writes x*scale.
Nothing outside but the two bitcast reshapes. VMEM: 2 in + 2 out buffers = 32 MB, limit 64 MB.
Speed idea: one HBM read + one write per element (537 MB), no relayout copies and no second read.

Grid (M/2048, N1/2048, K/512) = (2, 2, 8): x tile (2048, 512) f32, w1 tile (512, 2048) f32, both cast to bf16 in-kernel; acc (2048, 2048) f32 scratch; out (2048, 1024) f32 resident across j and k.
Each k step: 4 dots of (2048,512)@(512,512) bf16 with f32 acc into 512-lane slices of acc (bounded temporaries).
Last k: per 512-lane slice, per 128-lane column m = max(h, roll(h,-1)); m = max(m, roll(m,-2)) puts each window-of-4 max at lane 4q; bf16(m) @ S(512,128) one-hot selector compacts lanes exactly; concat 4 slices -> pooled (2048, 512) bf16 @ w2 rows [j*512, (j+1)*512) -> += out.
Nothing outside the kernel; x and w1 streamed twice each (256 MB) instead of an extra w1 transpose/cast pass; bf16 MXU inputs, f32 accumulation like XLA default.

Grid (Hp/8,) over 8-row strips of the first pooled map; x is reshaped to (B*C, H/2, 2W), so the first pool's row step is a max of two aligned lane halves, with no strided loads.
Halo rows come from the neighbouring 8-row blocks. The column pool and conv shifts use a 0/1 selection matmul (bf16), and the conv is one banded-weight matmul per batch item (f32 accumulation).
The weight rows are ordered so the second max-pool, bias and ReLU give (co,h2)-ordered rows. They are stored contiguously in a 2-D VMEM scratch with a 128-wide last dimension.
The linear layer accumulates into a (B,OUT) f32 scratch across the grid. It gathers features with strided row loads from that 2-D scratch.
Outside the kernel there are only stack, pad, concatenate, transpose, reshape, broadcast and astype on the weights and inputs.

Grid over row blocks of the input viewed as (-1, last_dim). When the last dim is a multiple of 128, this view should be a free reshape, avoiding the relayout copy that a 1024-lane reshape would likely cause. Otherwise it falls back to flat padding to 1024 lanes.
Blocks are about 2 MiB, (4096, 128) f32 here, giving 32 steps; 2 inputs x 2 buffers is about 8 MiB of VMEM. Rows past the end of a partial last block are masked with iota.
Each element is computed as log cosh(d) = d + log(1 + exp(-2d)) - log2 in f32, with d = |a - b| + eps, and summed into an (8, cols) f32 VMEM scratch.
On the last step the kernel reduces the scratch, scales by 1/n and writes a (1, 1) output. Outside the kernel only reshape, pad and astype are used.
Not run or timed yet.

Grid (rows // tm,) over the (B*C*H, W) bitcast view, tm = 4096 rows (4 MiB f32 per input block, 16 MiB double-buffered), "arbitrary".
Inside a step, fori_loop over 32-row chunks: atan(x) - atan(y), square, fold into an (8, W) f32 carry; the chain stays in vregs.
atan: Cephes range reduction with an EUP approximate reciprocal plus one Newton step, then a degree-9 odd polynomial.
(8, W) f32 VMEM accumulator across the grid; the last step reduces it and writes sqrt(sum / n) as a (1, 1) output.
Outside the kernel: only the leading-dim reshape and the final (1, 1) -> () reshape.

Reshape (N,C,H,W) -> (N*C,H,W) outside (layout only); grid over channel blocks of bc channels (~2 MiB f32 per block), block (bc,H,W), "parallel".
Reductions go over H (sublane/cross-vreg, mostly elementwise VPU work) first, then a single lane reduce on a (bc,1,W) slab. A (bc,H*W) layout would need a full lane reduce on every row.
Everything is computed in float32: max, exp(g*(x-m)), sum, then log. Output block (bc,1,1) is reshaped to (N,C,1,1) outside.
Speed idea: the kernel is HBM-bound at 128 MiB. Bigger blocks (64 grid steps) plus cheap sublane reductions should keep the VPU/XLU below DMA time. vmem_limit is raised to 64 MiB for the temporaries.

Grid (rows/8192,), input block (8192, 128) f32 of x.reshape(-1, 128) (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); output (rows/128, 128) f32, lane dense.
Inside, fori over 1024-row chunks: subtract the chunk mean (variance is shift invariant), one bf16 MXU dot [y | y*y] (1024, 256) @ block-diagonal ones (256, 256) with f32 accumulation.
Row i = 128g+8q+r of a chunk sits in sublane r: keep lane 16g+q and sum over the (g, q) vreg axes (VPU adds, no cross-lane work) -> one lane-dense (8,128) tile; var = (s2 - s1^2/d)/(d-1), clip, log in f32 on it.
Outside: only a reshape/transpose of the 2 MB result that undoes the (r, g, q) packing, to x.shape[:-1] + (1,).
Speed idea: no XLU transposes, a single MXU pass, compute well under the HBM read time, 64 grid steps.

Keep the native 4D layout (n, c, h, w). An (n, c, h*w) reshape would force XLA to insert a relayout copy of both 128 MB inputs.
Grid (n, h//th), both axes parallel. Input blocks are (1, c, th, w) for preds and target, with th picked so a block is about 2 MiB (th=16 here). 2 inputs x 2 buffers is about 8 MiB of VMEM.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop over channels (unroll 8) does clip, multiply and add into a float32 (th, w) accumulator. Summing over the leading axis needs only VPU adds, with no cross-sublane reduction.
At the end of each step the kernel stores -log(sum / c) into the (1, th, w) block of the (n, h, w) output. Nothing runs outside the kernel. The kernel is memory-bound, so it should stream close to HBM bandwidth.

layer 3 is not an NT dot_general (W3^T @ h2^T), which would make Mosaic transpose every
(512,144) bf16 h2 chunk and load it as MXU weights, and there is no 256-iteration serial fori_loop (no overlap between chunks).
each grid step takes 16 row-blocks of cs=1024 rows (x block (16384,128) bf16, 32 steps), packs 4 row-blocks side by side
by lane-concat (K=512, block-diagonal W1/W2), runs the 3 layers as plain row-streaming MXU dots in 4 independent groups,
and writes layer 3 for all 16 row-blocks into distinct columns of one (cs,128) f32 tile: ONE small f32 transpose per step
gives a lane-dense (16, cs) output block already in row order, so the output needs only a free reshape outside.

Keep the 4D layout (no reshape to H*W, which would cost a relayout copy in HBM). Grid (B, H//th), blocks (1, C, th, W) with th a multiple of 8 and C*th*W*4 <= 2 MiB (th=32 here), double-buffered for about 8 MiB total.
Inside the kernel, a fori_loop walks 8-row chunks. For each chunk, pass 1 takes the max over C, which is an elementwise max across vregs. Pass 2 accumulates s=Σe, Σe², Σe·t and Σt² in registers. The chunk's loss is Σe²/s² − 2Σet/s + Σt², so softmax probabilities are never written out.
All math is f32. A (rows, W) VMEM scratch holds the running sum across the grid, and the last step writes total/n to a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel there is only the scalar index.
Speed idea: avoid the HBM relayout copy and keep the per-element work light, so the kernel is limited by memory bandwidth.

Flatten only the leading dims: (B*C*H, W). With W=128 this keeps the (8,128) tiled layout, so no relayout copy happens outside the kernel (a reshape to a last dim of 1024 would cause one).
Grid (rows//bm,), with bm up to 8192 rows (4 MiB per input block), "arbitrary" semantics, vmem limit 64 MiB.
Inside each step, a fori_loop walks 256-row chunks; each chunk computes the masked squared difference and folds it into an (8, W) f32 carry. The carry is added to a VMEM scratch accumulator.
The last step does the full reduce and scales by 1/n into a (1,1) output. Outside the kernel there is only reshape and astype.

Grid (B*C*H/8192,) sequential, blocks (8192, 256) bf16 = 4 MiB per input, double-buffered (16 MiB).
Inner fori_loop over 64-row chunks: bf16 subtract, f32 square, fold into an (8, 256) f32 carry; f32 scratch accumulator across steps.
Outside: only the bitcast reshape to (B*C*H, W) and the final (1,1)->() reshape/astype.
Speed idea: no relayout copies (a (rows,512) reshape would triple HBM traffic); one read of each input at HBM rate.

Grid (rows/br,) "arbitrary" over the free view (B*D1*D2, D3); blocks (br, D3) of pred and real, br*D3*4 = 4 MB.
f32 scratch accumulator (8, D3): each step adds sum over row-groups of (real-pred)^2 using only elementwise vreg adds.
Last step: one full reduce of the (8, D3) partial, times 1/numel, written to a (1,1) output; outside only the bitcast reshape and [0,0].
Speed idea: no relayout copies, single HBM read of both inputs, no per-step cross-lane reduction.

Outside the kernel there are only layout ops: slice channels 0:2 and move the channel axis to the front. y_pred becomes (2,T,N) and y_gt becomes (2,N,T), both still bf16. This replaces the 128-lane-padded minor dim of 4 (my assumption about the layout; I could not run this) with compact, lane-dense arrays.
The grid is (T/bt, N/bn) with bt=bn=512 (or the largest divisor of the size that is a multiple of 128). The pred block is (2,bt,bn) and the gt block is (2,bn,bt), so each input block is 1 MiB and about 4 MiB with double buffering.
In the kernel, both blocks are cast to f32. The gt block is transposed on the XLU, then subtracted from the pred block, squared and summed over the two channels. Partial sums go into an (8,bn) f32 VMEM accumulator.
At the last grid step the kernel reduces the accumulator to a scalar and multiplies by 1/(T*N). Outside, the result is only reshaped and cast to bf16.
Why this should be faster: there is no lane-interleaving reshape relayout and no one-hot selection matmuls. What is left is one cheap XLA transpose copy per input and a kernel that reads 64 MB.

Grid (B//bb,) over batch, "arbitrary"; v block (bb, L, F) bf16 with bb*L*F ~ 1M elements (2 MiB block, 4 MiB double-buffered).
In kernel: x2 = x*x in bf16, then a batched NT matmul ones(bb,8,F) x x2 -> (bb,8,L) f32 sums of squares, which puts the L axis on lanes. Then sqrt and the margin terms in f32.
Labels go through scalar prefetch (SMEM). The one-hot is a per-row lane-iota == label select, applied as a correction on top of the all-negative term.
The f32 (8,L) VMEM accumulator is resident across the grid. The last step writes sum/(8*B) to the (1,1) output.
Outside the kernel: only labels passed as-is and the final reshape/astype. Speed: one bf16 matmul, no f32 upcast of the input, no hi/lo split, and few, large steps.

Grid over L only: (cdiv(L, TL),), with TL a multiple of 128 so each output block (B, nb, TL) is about 4 MiB (TL = 16384 at this config).
Mask block is (B, TL) and seq is a full (nb, 1) block. The output (B, nb, L) is written directly in its final layout, so no reshape or relayout copies are needed outside the kernel.
In the kernel: c = mask == 1, then for each row i, out[i] = where(c[i:i+1], seq_col, 0), broadcast to (nb, TL). No matmul, so no accumulator.
Outside the kernel there is only seq.reshape(nb, 1). A reshape of the 512 MiB output would most likely force a relayout copy.

Inputs viewed as (B*C*H, W) = (131072, 256) (leading-dim merge only, a bitcast); grid (rows/2048,) "arbitrary", three (2048, 256) f32 blocks = 2 MiB each.
Inner fori_loop over 32-row chunks computes the SmoothL1 terms in vregs and folds them into an (8, 256) f32 carry; per step the carry is added to a VMEM scratch.
Last step reduces the (8, 256) scratch to the mean in a (1, 1) f32 output; only the reshape to () and dtype cast stay outside.
Speed idea: one HBM read of the three inputs with no relayout copies, compute hidden under DMA.

The output is 3-D (B*C, 1, 2H) with block (cb, 1, 2H) (last two dims = full dims), so the per-channel loop index c
indexes the leading, untiled dim (o_ref[c, :, 0:H]); stores land at lane offsets 0 and H=128, both tile-aligned. With a (cb, 2H) out block, `o_ref[pl.ds(c, 1), ...]` would be a dynamic store at sublane row c, unaligned to the (8,128) tile, which Mosaic rejects.
x viewed as (B*C, H, W), block (cb, H, W) f32 (~4 MiB), fold W's 128-lane slabs (max, count of x>0),
transpose (XLU) and reduce over sublanes so H lands on lanes; count/W in-kernel. Outside: only reshapes. One HBM pass over x.

Grid over B*C in blocks of cb=8 channels. Each input block is (cb, H/2, 2W) f32 and each output block is (cb, H/2, W/2). That is about 5 MiB of VMEM with double buffering.
Outside the kernel, x.reshape(B*C, H/2, 2W) puts row pair (2i, 2i+1) side by side. Even rows are lanes [:W] and odd rows are lanes [W:], so no strided loads are needed.
Inside the kernel, a static loop over the cb channels works on 2D (H/2, W) tiles. Row 2i-1 comes from rolling the odd rows down by one sublane and masking the first row. Columns c-1 and c+1 come from lane rolls with a mask at column 0.
To keep only the even columns, the kernel multiplies by a one-hot (W, W/2) matrix. The f32 value is split into bf16 hi and lo parts, giving about 2^-17 relative error, with f32 accumulation.
The kernel is bound by HBM traffic (about 335 MB moved), and the matmul FLOPs are small next to that. The only work outside the kernel is reshapes.

Grid (h/hb, c/cb + 1), channel axis inner and "arbitrary". Input block (n, cb, hb, w), about 2 MiB (cb=8, hb=32), so each DMA chunk is 16 KB contiguous.
The output is 4D (n, c+1, h, w) with block (n, cb, hb, w). Channel is a leading dim, so cb needs no alignment, and the extra step k = c/cb writes the edge block holding channel c. Pallas masks the out-of-bounds rows on write.
When k < c/cb, the kernel copies the x block to the output and adds that block's per-channel batch std (two-pass, f32) into a (hb, w) f32 VMEM scratch. On the last step it writes acc/c broadcast over n.
x is read from HBM once and the output written once (about 512 MB). Nothing runs outside the kernel.

Grid (in_f/1024,) arbitrary: x block (B,1024) bf16, T2 block (1024, kd*out_f) bf16, matmul accumulated in a resident (B, kd*out_f) f32 scratch; x copied into the resident (B, in_f+out_f) output block each step.
Last step: pairwise L1 with loops j (8-row aligned groups, static row r) outer and i (8-row chunks) inner; row j of each k slab is broadcast once and reused; exp(-norm) accumulated into a (B,out_f) f32 scratch; o_b - 1 stored at lane offset in_f.
Outside: transpose/reshape of T to (in_f, kd*out_f) so every k is a lane-aligned 128-column slab (layout op).
No dynamic unaligned single-row loads, which Mosaic does not compile.

One pallas_call, grid (C+1,) = (257,); in block (N, 1, H, W) = (16, 1, 128, 128) f32 = 1 MiB at channel min(j, C-1); out block (N, 1, H, W) at channel j of the (N, C+1, H, W) output.
Steps j < C copy the block through and add sqrt(var_N + alpha) (N is a leading axis, so mean/var are elementwise) into an (H, W) f32 scratch.
Step C writes the broadcast global mean; its input index repeats that of step C-1, so no extra DMA.
No reshape anywhere: the output is produced directly in its final NCHW layout.
Speed idea: x is read once (268 MB) and the output written once (269 MB); no second read of x and no relayout copies.

Flatten only the leading dims: (8*128*128, 256). This keeps the TPU tiled layout, so no relayout copy is needed (a reshape to 1024 lanes would likely force copies outside the kernel).
Grid over rows with blocks of 2048x256 f32 (2 MiB each): 2 inputs + 1 output, double-buffered, is about 12 MiB. vmem_limit is raised to 48 MiB.
The math is done in f32 inside the kernel and cast on store. The grid axis is marked parallel. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes.

Merge only the leading dims: x.reshape(L, H, W) leaves the tiled (H, W) layout alone, so no relayout copy is needed (a (rows, 1024) reshape would force copies on input and output).
Grid (L/b,), block (b, H, W): full trailing dims, b is the largest divisor of L with block size <= 4 MiB.
The multiply is done in f32 inside the kernel and cast on store. Outside the kernel there are only reshapes.
vmem_limit is raised to 48 MiB, since 4 MiB blocks for input and output, double-buffered, take 16 MiB. The grid axis is parallel.

Reshape x,y (layout only) from (B,C,H,W) to (B*C*H/16, 16*W). Each row then holds 16 consecutive image rows, so pooling rows means adding 1024-lane-aligned slices. That avoids a strided sublane load, which Mosaic rejects.
Grid: (rows/32,), blocks of (32, 16*W) bf16, sequential "arbitrary" axis. A float32 (5, 8, W) VMEM accumulator is resident across the grid, and the last step writes a (1,1) float32 result.
Pooling is linear, so the kernel takes d = x - y once and builds a 4-level pairwise tree: row pairs come from slice adds, column pairs from a lane roll by 2^(k-1). Columns stay dilated, and the last step keeps only lanes j % 2^k == 0.
Sums fold onto 8 sublanes with VALU adds only. Each level does half the work of the one before, so total VALU work stays close to the HBM-bound cost of reading 256 MiB.
Outside the kernel: only the reshapes and the final [0,0] slice plus astype.

Grid (B, H/Hb), blocks (1, C, Hb, W) of the native array, Hb chosen for ~2 MB (Hb=16 here), f32 math.
Softmax over the leading block axis C: max and sum are elementwise across vregs, no cross-lane work.
One reciprocal per (h, w) pixel, then a multiply per element.
Nothing outside the kernel. Speed: one HBM read + write with no relayout copies.

Grid (B, H/64) "arbitrary"; x block (C, 64, W) bf16 = 2 MiB on the native 4D array; output block (ob, O, 64, W) bf16 = 4 MiB of the native 5D output; ~13 MiB VMEM double-buffered, limit 64 MiB.
Step (0,0) builds kron(w, I_16) (O*16, C*16) bf16 in VMEM scratch, w = v * g / ||v|| computed in f32 in-kernel.
Per 16-row chunk: x (C,16,W) merged to (C*16, W) for free, one MXU dot (256x2048 @ 2048x128) with f32 accumulation, cast to bf16, add each SMEM bias in bf16 and store ob copies.
Outside the kernel: bias reshape/astype only; no relayout of x or the output ((.., H*W) views would cost two copies).
Speed idea: the op is bound by the 64 MiB output write; 16x redundant MXU FLOPs are cheap.

Outside: predict.reshape(-1, W) (merge leading dims only, bitcast; W = 128 lanes). Output (1, 1) reshaped to ().
Grid (rows // br,), arbitrary (sequential reduction); block (br, W) with br = 8192 rows (4 MiB f32).
Inner fori over 64-row chunks: mask = p < thr, loss = where(mask, log(1 - p + eps), 0), fold rows to (8, W) and add.
f32 accumulators (8, W) for loss and mask count in VMEM scratch; last step reduces both and writes -loss / count.
Speed idea: no relayout copy, so HBM traffic is one read of the input, like XLA.

Grid (M/4096,), x block (4096, 256) bf16 of the bitcast view (M, K); weights and biases resident (constant index maps).
Both matmuls on the MXU with f32 accumulation; each result is cast to bf16 once, then bias add / relu run in bf16 (v6e VPU has bf16),
matching the reference's bf16 rounding points.
Outside: reshape of x to (M, K) (leading-dim merge, a bitcast) and of the biases to rows.
Speed: 32 large steps instead of 128 to cut per-step overhead; half the epilogue vregs.

Grid (B/8,) parallel; x phase-deinterleaved outside (layout transpose) to (B*C, 16*H/4*W/4) so 2x2 pools become lane-block maxes.
conv1: block-diagonal (8*C1, 9*8*C padded to 256) bf16 weight @ rolled+masked patch slabs, f32 acc, max over the 4 pool phases, tanh.
conv2: 9 taps of block-diagonal (8*C2, 8*C1) bf16 weights @ rolled phase slabs, f32 acc, pool max, tanh; fc1/fc2 in f32 HIGHEST.
Outside: only reshape/transpose/pad/concatenate/broadcast/astype on x and weights (no jnp.tile).

Conv call: grid (256/16,) over groups of 16 fc rows (64 images); input block (121, 4, 16, 128) bf16 = images as matmul rows, width on lanes.
conv1 = Toeplitz matmul (256, 640) @ (640, 3840) per 2 pooled rows, 2x2 max-pool by row-parity / column-parity halves, bias+ReLU, kept in a (58, 64, 2048) bf16 VMEM scratch;
  conv2 = (960, 1536) @ (1536, 384) per pooled row with 3x3 pool on row/lane slices; f32 accumulate, bf16 features out (18, 256, 2560).
FC call: grid (18,) reduction over pooled rows into a (256, 64) f32 scratch, ReLU, then (64, 136) matmul in the last step.
Outside: only transposes/pads/reshapes and broadcasts building the Toeplitz weights (no jnp.tile). Speed idea: conv1/conv2 intermediates (~0.9 GB in XLA) never touch HBM.

Grid over batch tiles of BT=8 images, parallel; whole net fused in one kernel per tile.
Activations are width-blocks of shape (H*BT, P*C); each conv+relu+pool is one bf16 matmul against a banded (Toeplitz) weight, accumulated in f32. Horizontal pool takes the max of two lane halves, vertical pool the max over a leading axis.
FC1 sums one matmul per pooled row; FC2 uses a block-diagonal weight; all accumulation is f32.
Outside the kernel: only pad/reshape/transpose/broadcast_to/concatenate/astype to rebuild the weights (tiling done with broadcast_to+reshape).

Grid (B/64,), block of 64 boards (64, 8, 1152): each board is a (C, P) slab with pixel (h,w) on lane (h+1)*33+w and zero borders.
Per board (fori_loop): 3x3 convs as 9 lane rolls concatenated to (9C, P) and one bf16 MXU matmul (f32 acc), ReLU and border mask;
1x1 heads (8, P) written into 9 separate (512,128) VMEM slabs (128-lane base so strided loads lower).
Then per head channel a stride-8 gather (64, 1152) @ board-padded fc weights; log_softmax and value MLP + tanh in f32.
Outside: pad/reshape of x into the board layout, weight transposes/pads/astype. Speed: x read once, all activations stay in VMEM.

Trunk call: grid (B/8,) "parallel"; per step two sub-batches of 4 images with spatial (4*1024) in lanes; 3x3 convs as im2col by
lane rolls x edge masks, one bf16 MXU dot per layer (Cout, 9*Cin) @ (9*Cin, 4096), f32 accumulation, bias + relu; both 1x1 heads
in one dot; writes the NCHW-flattened policy (B, 4*1024) and value (B, 2*1024) maps in f32.
FC call: grid (B/1024, 4096/1024) with an f32 output-resident accumulator for the policy logits; value MLP + tanh at k == 0.
Log-softmax over the batch axis: a third call, grid over 128-lane column blocks with the whole batch resident.
Outside: one relayout reshape of x to (B, C, H*W) padded to 8 channels, weight transposes/pads/astype.

Grid (B, C/Cb), Cb=16: blocks (1,16,256,256) f32 = 4 MB in and out, double-buffered 16 MB (vmem limit raised to 48 MB).
Elementwise f32: round(x*255), clip [0,255], * (1/255). No reshape or copy outside the kernel.
Speed idea: one read and one write of the native layout; large blocks keep the per-step overhead small (64 steps).

Grid (B/8,) "parallel" on the native (B, L) array; in/out blocks (8, L) f32 = 8 MB each (full rows, so min/max are local).
Inside: fori over 2048-lane chunks keeping an (8, 2048) running max/min, one lane reduction to (8, 1), then a second fori
writing (x - min) * (2 / (max - min + eps)) - 1. All f32; no cross-step accumulator.
Outside: nothing; the kernel reads and writes the native layout.
Speed idea: no (B, L/128, 128) reshape, which would cost relayout copies on both sides; one HBM read + one write of 134 MB each.

Reshape x to (B*C, H, W). Merging leading dims is free; a (-1, 1024) reshape would change the tiled minor dims and force relayout copies on the input and the output.
Grid (B*C // tb,), block (tb, H, W) with tb*H*W*2 bytes about 2 MiB (tb=16 here), dimension marked parallel.
w1 and w2 are cast to f32 and passed through SMEM as scalars. Inside the kernel x is upcast to f32, the PLU formula is applied, and the result is cast back to bf16 on store.
Nothing outside the kernel except reshape and astype. vmem_limit raised to 64 MiB to cover the f32 temporaries.
Speed idea: a single streaming pass at HBM bandwidth with no extra layout copies.
